title: Stop Trying to Fix People
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article draws a sharp distinction between coaching behavior and trying to 'fix' personality, arguing the second is both futile and relationally damaging. It explains that traits rooted in biology and stable personality — like introversion — change only at the margins over a lifetime, while behaviors, habits, and tactical skills remain highly coachable regardless of underlying personality. Leaders who try to fix deep personality traits, the piece argues, make people feel scrutinized without producing real change, whereas focusing on behavior change produces results. It also acknowledges a hard edge: some personality traits are simply disqualifying for team performance and should be screened for in hiring, not addressed after the fact through coaching.
points: Personality traits rooted in biology, like introversion, are highly resistant to change and shift only marginally over a lifetime.
Behavior, habits, and tactics — unlike personality — remain genuinely coachable regardless of a person's underlying traits.
Leaders who try to 'fix' personality rather than change behavior tend to damage the relationship without producing real change.
Some personality traits are disqualifying for team performance and should be caught in hiring/selection, not treated as a coaching problem later.
quotes: A leader’s role is to change how people act, engage, and respond to make them more effective while at the same time accepting that many of their flaws and failings can’t be influenced or modified.
Personality traits, like introversion, are relatively stable throughout adulthood.
Leaders who attempt to “fix” qualities rooted in biology and personality are doomed to fail and make the target of their repairs feel scrutinized and disfavored.
Team members with high anxiety, emotional instability, low self-discipline, and the need to dominate, among other traits, likely render themselves incapable of performing on a team.
It’s time to change your approach. Stop trying to fix people. Coach them up instead.
